From: Sam Ellison <sam.ellison@greenwave.io>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: OneTrust presign + service-account evidence request

Hi Chloe & Ben,

We're finalising our OneTrust onboarding and the security team needs a couple of things to complete the profile:

- A presigned-manifest (CSV) format example and the S3 prefix we should upload to.
- Evidence of the service account used for automated uploads (audit log snippet showing the account operating against the target bucket).
- A simple IAM role-to-user mapping for any service accounts you expect OneTrust to read from (so our internal audit can reconcile).

Can you confirm whether a 24-hour presign TTL is acceptable and whether you prefer us to upload to a per-tenant path or a shared path? Attaching our onboarding checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Ellison
Security Operations Manager, GreenWave Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>

Sam — thanks for the clear checklist.

Short answers up front: a 24-hour presign TTL is fine for the initial upload window; we prefer a per-tenant path (s3://redwood-onetrust/uploads/greenwave/).

I'll loop in Jonas from Integrations to provide the exact manifest format and an example IAM mapping. Ben, can you confirm any retention/ttl notes for presigned manifests?

Items I'll action:
- Confirm manifest CSV columns + sample row (Jonas)
- Pull the service-account audit snippet from CloudTrail for the last 30 days (Ben)
- Share a small example presign_manifest.csv so GreenWave can validate their uploader flow (me/Ben)

Chloe Martin
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sam Ellison <sam.ellison@greenwave.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust presign + service-account evidence request

Adding the manifest & role mapping details below — attaching the IAM mapping spreadsheet.

Manifest (minimal CSV columns):
- object_key, size_bytes, uploaded_at_iso8601, checksum_sha256, source_agent_id

Example row:
redwood-onetrust/uploads/greenwave/20261118/manifest-0001.json, 12345, 2026-11-18T17:02:00Z, e3b0c442..., greenwave-uploader-01

On service accounts: OneTrust will need a read/list permission against the tenant prefix. Our preferred pattern is to create a dedicated read-only service account (serviceAccount:onetrust-reader@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com) and restrict it to the single prefix. For audit evidence, we can export a CloudTrail filter for events where userIdentity.arn contains the service account.

Attached: iam_mapping.xlsx — contains mapping columns: internal_principal, principal_type, expected_prefix, notes.

I'll prepare a short presign TTL recommendation (24 hours for initial ingest; 7 days only if mature and using retries + signed upload policy).

Jonas Weber
Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: iam_mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks all — quick update and a sample manifest attached.

- We've scoped a per-tenant path: s3://redwood-onetrust/uploads/greenwave/ (as Chloe noted).
- Attached presign_manifest.csv is an example payload you can run through your client. It contains two lines (one sample manifest row + header).
- Presign TTL: 24h default. If GreenWave wants a longer window while they troubleshoot, we can issue a 72h presign on request but prefer 24h for security.
- Audit snippet: I've exported the CloudTrail entries showing the service account calling PutObject/ListBucket on the prefix; Sam, I'll share a redacted PDF via the Drive link to avoid sending raw logs in email.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-presign-manifests
